rule: docs/TREE_PLAN.md: one yard tree for every two or three houses, in back yards and at lot corners, never against a fence or a wall (zone 813 -> about 400)
written: by hand, 19 Nov 2026 (cloud session, the city-wide superchecker run from the bottom of the list). The quadrant's seventeen builder trees go (a row of ficus, jacarandas and corals every 6-7 m along the back fences, one 3 m from a house front, a few in the yards inside the wrought-iron fence); five come back on their own spots, about one for every two houses: by the swing set, the open lot corner, and in yards 7-12 m from the houses.

trees.why: the west back yard with the swing set (2.6 m off): shade over the swings
the open lot corner inside the wrought-iron fence, 27 m from the walls: a full magnolia
the yard south of it, 12 m from the house: the yard's tree, 31 m from the magnolia
the middle yard by the bird of paradise, 12.5 m from the house
the east back yard of the south row, 7 m from the house: the one tree of the old back fence row (one every 6 m)
